title: W2 DRAFT: ratios for the audit-born norms against their real homes (F6, U2, U4, F1, U1, U3)
description: Wave 2 is where the mandate's own framing is wrong, and the records must not repeat the error. F1, F6, U1, U2, U3 and U4 are not a peer set - they are audit_gen3.md's internal finding numbers, with three different fates. F6 became a standing ORCHESTRATION.md rule AND is already codified as PR-004 (nothing to mint). U2 and U4 became ORCHESTRATION.md rules with P-number anchors. F1 never generalized past the single fix it produced and lives as a planner convention in .harness/plan.md. U1 and U3 live ONLY in .claude/agents/orchestration-planner.md (U3 also appears downstream in AGENTS.md and the context-scout definition). A record that gives F1 or U1 the standing F6 earned is a falsified ledger, and the scout's section 2.5 names that asymmetry as a live risk. You draft the ratios; a verifier confirms them against source.

INPUT IS THE FROZEN LEDGER's wave-2 rows, exactly as frozen; a row added, dropped or re-tiered is a DEVIATION: note naming the row, the reason and the new N2. FOR EVERY ROW, THREE ARTIFACTS SIDE BY SIDE: the SOURCE TEXT quoted verbatim with path and section; the RATIO as it will be published; the COMPLETE publish command with no ellipsis, ratio via --ratio-file (P-021).

REACH IS STATED IN EVERY RATIO - this is the wave's whole point. Each record says WHO it binds and WHERE the duty lives: U1's and U3's reach is the planner's agent-definition file (and, for U3, the downstream feeds), not ORCHESTRATION.md; F1's reach is a planner convention with one audit finding behind it, never generalized. The tier and the ratio must make that asymmetry with PR-004 visible rather than flattening the six labels into one peer set.

F6 IS ALREADY CODIFIED AS PR-004: do not re-mint it under any subject. If wave 2 needs to connect to it, the mechanism is a follows or cites relation from a new record, never a second record for the same norm. The ORCHESTRATION.md marker for PR-004 is T-386's job.

STALE LINE ANCHORS ARE A KNOWN, MEASURED TRAP: ORCHESTRATION.md:80 and audit_gen3.md cite state.json:352/356/358 for F6/U2/U4 and those exact lines no longer point at that content. No ratio may repeat a stale line anchor. VALIDITY CONDITIONS THAT ACTUALLY CHECK: stale's check V only evaluates validity entries in file-line or bare-path form (.harness/bin/precedent.py _validity_entry_checkable_kind); free text is reported unchecked and never flagged. Give each record at least one CHECKABLE validity entry naming the file the norm's home lives in - for U1/U3 that is the agent-definition file, which is the honest anchor and also the thing that would have to move for the norm to change.

CD6 - TIER EVIDENCE HONESTLY: U2 and U4 have P-number anchors (P-016/P-017) and can carry them; F1, U1 and U3 do not, and the records say so and take the tier their evidence supports. An audit-file finding is a real, git-verifiable anchor - cite the file and section, not a line number.
CD3 - P-023 untouched, and no record may propose a state.json write. CD5 - nothing minted for a NOT-CODIFIED row; settled history goes in dicta if anywhere.
SCOPE_CONDITIONS role-shaped; no self-confirmation; title <= 80 chars with the count stated; subject slug unique against the live registry.
